# Detection rules

<!-- generated by scripts/lib/gen-catalogue.mjs; do not edit by hand -->

91 rules. Severity weights: critical 12, major 6, minor 2 points.
Each extra occurrence adds 25% of the weight, capped at 2x. Score = sum of points, max 100.
Verdict: **heavy** at 35 or more; **clean** below 10 with no critical finding; otherwise **light**.

Where: `desktop` = 1440 px, `mobile` = 390 px, `css` rules read the stylesheet text.

## spacing

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spacing-off-grid` | minor | desktop | Padding and gaps ignore a 4 px rhythm. Values like 13, 18 or 22 px show that spacing was typed, not chosen from a scale. | Pick a 4 px scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64) and snap every padding and gap to the nearest step. |
| `spacing-cramped` | minor | desktop+mobile | Text sits against the edge of its box. Buttons and cards with almost no inner padding read as unfinished. | Give buttons at least 12 px horizontal and 8 px vertical padding (anything under 8 px horizontal is flagged), cards at least 16 px. |

## color

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color-purple-gradient` | critical | desktop | Violet / indigo gradient. The purple-to-blue gradient is the most recognisable AI-product colour move. | Replace with one flat brand colour. If depth is needed, use a surface step and a 1 px line, not a gradient. |
| `color-gradient-text` | major | desktop | Gradient-filled text. Headings or numbers clipped to a colour ramp are a stock "AI landing" signature. | Set the text in one solid colour; emphasise with size, weight or position instead. |
| `color-glow` | major | desktop | Coloured glow shadow. Large zero-offset shadows in a saturated colour fake "energy" and hurt legibility. | Use a neutral, low-alpha shadow with a real offset, or no shadow and a 1 px border. |
| `color-low-contrast` | major | desktop+mobile | Text below WCAG contrast. Grey-on-tint and pale-on-white text fails readers and audits alike. | Darken the text (or lighten the surface) until body text reaches 4.5:1 and large text 3:1. |
| `color-framework-default` | major | desktop | Stock framework palette. Untouched indigo/violet/slate swatches from popular utility palettes make unrelated products look alike. | Derive the palette from the brand: one accent chosen on purpose, neutrals tinted toward it. |
| `color-random-gradient` | major | desktop | Gradient across unrelated hues. A ramp that jumps across more than 120 degrees of hue (orange to teal to pink) has no brand logic. | Use one hue family, or a flat colour. |
| `color-rainbow` | major | desktop | Rainbow of series colours in a chart. Every bar or slice in a different hue implies categories that are not there. | One colour for the data, a second only to highlight the item that matters. |
| `color-accent-decorative` | minor | desktop | Accent colour spent on decoration. When the accent paints rules, tags and ornaments, it no longer tells the reader what to press or what changed. | Keep the accent for actions, selection, focus, live state and the key data series. Decoration goes neutral. |
| `color-faded-heading-part` | major | desktop+mobile | Half of the heading greyed out. A heading whose second clause or last word is set in pale grey at the same size ("Took hours. Now one search.") is a stock template move; the pale half fails contrast and the ranking it implies is not real. | Set the whole heading in the text colour. If one part matters less, cut it or move it into the paragraph; if it matters more, change the words, not the grey. |
| `color-faded-text` | major | desktop+mobile | Faded support text. Light grey support text that passes the bare minimum still reads as faded; it is the "muted subtitle" look of generated pages and tires the eye. | Readable text at 7:1 or more (4.5:1 from 24 px up). Rank with size and weight, not by greying text out. |
| `color-rainbow-tiles` | major | desktop | Every tile a different bright colour. A grid where each card gets its own saturated fill or gradient turns the page into a sweet shop; nothing ranks and the brand has no colour. | One surface colour for all tiles; let one accent mark the primary or selected tile. |

## icons

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `icon-tile` | major | desktop | Icon in a rounded coloured tile, repeated. A tinted square with a glyph above a heading is the default feature-card opener. | Drop the tile. Use a bare icon at one size, or no icon and let the heading carry the card. |
| `icon-emoji-ui` | major | desktop | Emoji used as interface icons. Emoji in headings, buttons and list items render differently per platform and signal a quick draft. | Use one consistent line-icon set (one size, one stroke width) or remove the glyph. |

## copy

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `copy-cliche` | major | desktop | Stock marketing vocabulary. Words such as "seamless", "elevate" or "unleash" carry no information and mark the text as generated. | Say the concrete thing: what the product does, for whom, with what number or example. |
| `copy-contrast-formula` | major | desktop | "Not X, but Y" headline formula. Defining the product by what it is not ("not just a tool, it's a partner") is a reflex of generated copy. | State the claim directly: say what it is and what the reader gets. |
| `copy-em-dash` | minor | desktop | Em dashes scattered through the copy. Three or more em dashes on one page is a frequent sign of generated prose. | Split the sentence, or use a comma, colon or full stop. |
| `copy-trailing-period` | minor | desktop | Full stops on short UI text. Headings, buttons and labels do not end in a full stop; paragraphs do. | Remove the final full stop from headings, buttons, labels and captions of one sentence. |
| `copy-greeting` | minor | desktop | Greeting as a page heading. "Welcome back, Sam" names no context; the heading should say what this screen is. | Name the content ("This month's scans"), not the visitor. |
| `copy-placeholder` | critical | desktop | Placeholder or filler text left in. Lorem ipsum, "Acme", "John Doe" and [bracketed] gaps show the page was never finished. | Write the real text, or remove the block. Never ship a stand-in name. |
| `copy-unverified-proof` | major | desktop | Social proof with no source. Round user counts, star scores and "trusted by" lines that cannot be checked read as invented. | Cite the source and date, link to the real logo or review, or delete the claim. |
| `copy-fake-data` | major | desktop | Stock fake names and data. Acme, Globex, John Doe and "User 1" are the placeholder cast of generated demos. | Use plausible, specific sample entries, and label them as sample data. |
| `copy-caption-sprawl` | major | desktop | Captions under everything. A small grey explanation under every block and visual, or the same "example data" note repeated, is filler that makes the page read as generated. | Let headings and visuals speak. Keep one honest example-data note per page (footer or one corner), not one per element. |
| `copy-emoji` | major | desktop | Emoji in the page. Emoji in headings, buttons, labels or body copy are the most visible AI tell. | Remove them. Use words, or one icon set drawn for the product. Keep emoji only if the brief says the user asked for them (<meta name="unslop-brief" content="emoji: reason">). |

## typography

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type-flat-hierarchy` | major | desktop | Flat type hierarchy. When the largest text is barely bigger than body text, nothing leads the eye. | Set a scale with clear steps: at least 2x between page title and body, and visible steps between heading levels. |
| `type-eyebrow` | major | desktop | Eyebrow label above the heading. A small, spaced, uppercase tag above every heading is a template habit. | Delete it, or fold the information into the heading. Keep at most one, and only if it carries a fact. |
| `type-tight-leading` | minor | desktop+mobile | Body text set too tight. Multi-line paragraphs under 1.3 line-height, or letter-spacing below -0.04em, are hard to read. | Body line-height 1.5 to 1.7; keep tight leading for headings only and never track tighter than -0.03em. |
| `type-long-measure` | minor | desktop | Line length above 85 characters. Very long lines make the eye lose its place. | Cap running text at 60 to 75 characters (max-width: 65ch). |
| `type-heavy-weight` | minor | desktop | Heavy weights carry the hierarchy. Weights of 800 to 900, or bold on most text, flatten emphasis. Hierarchy should come from size and colour. | Use 400 and 500 (600 sparingly). Let size and tone do the ranking. |
| `type-mono-outside-code` | minor | desktop | Monospace type used outside code. Monospace for labels, stats and dates is decoration that tries to look technical. | Keep monospace for code, paths and identifiers. Use the body family with tabular numbers for data. |
| `type-small-text` | minor | desktop+mobile | Several text elements under 13 px. Three or more small text elements make a page tiring to read, especially on phones. | Raise captions and labels to at least 13 px (body 16 px). |
| `type-tiny-text` | major | desktop+mobile | Text under 11 px. Text this small cannot be read by most people, even in an app. | Never go below 11 px; aim for 13 px or more. |
| `type-long-headline` | minor | desktop | Headline longer than two lines. A headline that needs three lines or more is a paragraph in disguise. | Cut it to one clear statement of at most two lines at desktop width. |
| `type-accent-keyword` | major | desktop | One word of the headline in the accent colour. Colouring or gradient-filling one keyword of the headline is the most common template tell, even on design-tool sites. | Let the whole headline speak in one colour. If a second tone is wanted, make it a quieter grey for a whole line, not a bright keyword. |
| `type-live-number-proportional` | minor | desktop | Changing numbers in proportional figures. Timers, prices and counters that update while set in proportional figures jitter sideways on every change. | Set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every number that changes (and on table columns of numbers). |
| `type-ai-default-font` | major | desktop | AI-default font. Display serifs and text faces that agents pick by reflex (the list in references/ai-default-fonts.md) make every generated page sound the same. | Choose a face for this project and write why in the brief. To keep a listed face on purpose, add <meta name="unslop-brief" content="font: Family, reason">. |
| `type-house-pairing` | major | desktop | Same type pairing as a previous project. Reusing the display and text pairing of the repo examples (or of your previous project) is a house style: every page starts to look like the last one, whatever the mood. | Pick a recipe from type/ that matches the brief's mood words and is not in scripts/lib/used-type.mjs; write its id and reason in the brief. To keep the pairing for a real project reason, add <meta name="unslop-brief" content="font: Family, reason">. |
| `type-hero-number` | major | desktop | Giant display number. A figure set at display size on its own ("€18,460", "99.9%") is the stock dashboard and landing move; size replaces meaning. | Put the number in a sentence with its comparison and date, at heading size, or chart it. |
| `type-heading-muted-subtitle` | major | desktop | Heading plus grey subtitle, section after section. A heading followed by a smaller, greyed paragraph in every section is the template rhythm of generated landing pages. | Let the section open with its content (a product view, a table, a list) or write one sentence in the main text colour. Vary how sections start. |

## layout

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layout-nested-cards` | major | desktop | Card inside a card. Boxes within boxes add borders and shadows but no information. | Keep one container. Group inside it with spacing, a divider or a heading. |
| `layout-identical-cards` | major | desktop | Row of identical icon + title + text cards. Three or four same-size feature cards in a row say nothing about which point matters. | Rank the points: one larger block for the main idea, the rest as a list or table. |
| `layout-stat-strip` | major | desktop | Row of big numbers with small labels. A strip of three or four headline metrics without a comparison is the standard hero-metric template. | Show one number that matters most, with its comparison base and date; move the rest into a table or chart. |
| `layout-side-stripe` | major | desktop | Coloured stripe down one side of a box. A thick left border on a card, alert or quote is a common AI shortcut for emphasis. | Emphasise with a tinted surface, a heading or an icon. Do not use a one-sided accent border. |
| `layout-overflow-x` | critical | desktop+mobile | Page scrolls sideways. Horizontal overflow is a bug, most often on phones. | Find the widest element, give it max-width: 100% or let it wrap; do not hide the overflow on body. |
| `layout-tap-target` | minor | mobile | Touch targets under 32 px. Small buttons and links are hard to hit on a phone. | Make every control at least 44 px tall (minimum 32 px) with padding rather than larger text. |
| `page-no-heading` | major | desktop | Page has no heading at all. Without any h1 to h6 the page has no outline for readers, search engines or screen readers. | Add one h1 that names the page, then h2 for each section. |
| `page-multiple-h1` | minor | desktop | More than one h1. Several h1 elements blur what the page is about. | Keep one h1; demote the others to h2. |
| `page-untitled-sections` | minor | desktop | Sections without a heading. Sections with no title cannot be scanned or navigated. | Give each section a heading (or aria-label if a visible one would be redundant). |
| `layout-text-at-edge` | major | desktop+mobile | Text glued to the screen edge. Copy that starts within 8 px of the viewport edge has no page margin. | Give the page container a side padding of at least 16 px on phones and 24 px on desktop. |
| `layout-empty-middle` | minor | desktop | Large empty band between content blocks. A gap of more than 320 px between two pieces of content reads as a broken or unfinished page. | Pull the blocks together, or fill the band with the content that belongs there. |
| `layout-one-sided-hero` | minor | desktop | First screen leans entirely to one side. On a wide screen all content sits in the left 60% and the right is empty, so the first view feels unbalanced. | Balance the first screen: put the key visual, product view or a second column opposite the text. |
| `layout-no-focal-point` | major | desktop | No focal point on the first screen. When no text is clearly larger than the rest and there is no large image, the eye has nowhere to start. | Make one element dominant: a headline at least 2x the body size, or a large product image. |
| `layout-late-headline` | minor | desktop | Main headline starts low on the screen. If the h1 begins below 60% of the first screen, the page opens on filler. | Move the headline into the upper half; trim the header and any banner above it. |
| `layout-side-nav-mobile` | major | mobile | Desktop side navigation on a phone. A fixed-width sidebar leaves a narrow strip for content on a 390 px screen. | Below 760 px, fold the sidebar away: show a header row with a menu toggle, or tabs pinned to the bottom of the screen. |
| `layout-uneven-rows` | minor | desktop | Table rows of different heights. Rows that differ in height make a table look broken and hard to scan. | Give rows one fixed padding and keep cell content to a single line (truncate, do not wrap). |
| `layout-text-overlap` | major | desktop+mobile | Text drawn on top of other text. Two pieces of text sharing the same spot cannot be read. It is usually an absolutely positioned label or a fixed height that broke on a narrow screen. | Give the elements their own space (grid, gap, wrapping), or put an opaque surface under the top layer if the overlap is intended. |
| `layout-stock-dark-launch` | major | desktop | Stock dark launch hero. Black hero, centred headline, one hot pill button and an install-command chip is the default component-library launch page; on a product that is not a developer tool it says nothing about the product. | Start from the project read: show the product, pick a combination for this audience, drop the install chip unless people really install it. |

## detail

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detail-pulse-dot` | major | desktop | Pulsing status dot. A blinking "live" dot on a status that never changes pretends the product is alive. | Show status only when it comes from data, as text plus colour, without animation. |
| `detail-glass` | minor | desktop | Frosted glass on several surfaces. Backdrop blur on many elements costs performance and rarely has anything meaningful behind it. | Use solid surfaces. Keep blur for at most one overlay that really sits over content. |
| `detail-announce-pill` | major | desktop | Announcement pill above the hero heading. A rounded "New: ..." badge above the h1 is on nearly every generated landing page. | Remove it. If there is real news, link it in the header or footer. |
| `detail-numbered` | minor | desktop | Decorative section numbers. "01 / 02 / 03" on content that has no sequence is ornament. | Number only real steps (use an ordered list). Otherwise drop the numbers. |
| `detail-arrow-links` | minor | desktop | Arrow glyph on many links. Appending "→" to every link and button is decoration. | Keep an arrow only on the single primary action, if direction carries meaning. |
| `detail-card-triple` | minor | desktop | Border, soft shadow and tint on every card. Stacking a border, a diffuse shadow and a different fill on the same surface is three signals for one idea. | Pick one separator per surface: a border, or a tint, or (for floating layers only) a shadow. |
| `detail-focus-ring` | major | css | Focus outline removed without a replacement. Keyboard users cannot see where they are. | Add :focus-visible with a 2 px outline (or ring) in an accent colour; never leave outline: none alone. |
| `detail-hover-lift` | minor | css | Cards lift or grow on hover. translateY(-4px) and scale(1.05) on hover is a stock micro-interaction. | Change tone or border colour on hover, only inside @media (hover: hover). |
| `detail-heavy-shadow` | minor | desktop | Heavy resting shadows. Large dark shadows on elements at rest make the page look puffy and dated. | Keep shadows only on floating layers (menus, dialogs) and make them subtle: low alpha, small blur. |
| `detail-version-badge` | minor | desktop | Version or BETA badge as decoration. A small "v2.0" or "BETA" pill near the top signals polish by label, not by substance. | Remove it unless the status changes what the reader can do; then say so in a sentence. |
| `detail-scroll-hint` | minor | desktop | "Scroll" hint. A scroll prompt or bouncing chevron admits the page does not invite scrolling by itself. | Let the next section peek above the fold instead. |
| `detail-fake-window` | major | desktop | Fake window chrome built from divs. Three red, yellow and green dots over a drawn "app" is a stand-in for a real product view. | Use a real screenshot or the real component, or drop the mock. |
| `a11y-no-name` | major | desktop | Control without an accessible name. Icon-only buttons, empty links and unlabeled inputs are announced as nothing by screen readers. | Add visible text, aria-label, or a <label> for every button, link and input. |
| `a11y-click-div` | major | desktop | Click handler on a non-interactive element. A div or span with onclick cannot be reached or activated from the keyboard. | Use a real <button> or <a href>. |
| `env-dev-server` | minor | desktop | Page is served by a dev server. Dev builds are slower, unminified and differ from production, so a score taken on them misleads. | Build for production and audit the built output (or the deployed URL). |
| `detail-showcase-ornament` | minor | desktop | Showcase effect with no job. Glow orbs, beams, spotlights, shimmer borders and particle fields dropped in as decoration: delete them and the message loses nothing. | Remove the effect, or tie it to content (light behind the product, a beam that follows a real data flow). |
| `detail-urgency-timer` | major | desktop+mobile | Countdown urgency. A ticking "10:21:05 left" next to a claim button is manufactured scarcity; on template and launch pages the deadline usually resets on every visit, and visitors know it. | Remove the timer. If an offer really ends, state the date and time once ("until 14 November, 18:00 CET") and keep it true. |
| `detail-paper-props` | major | desktop | Paper props as decoration. Cream paper cards, letter stacks, receipts, notebook rules and newsprint on a screen product are a costume, not the product. | Show the real interface surfaces of the product in its own colours. Drop ruled-paper backgrounds and cream sheets laid on a dark stage. |
| `detail-stamp-sticker` | major | desktop | Stamps and tilted stickers. Rubber stamps ("Paid", "Approved"), tilted badges and rotated sticker cards are props that stand in for real state. | Show state as text plus colour in the interface itself, upright. Remove rotation from cards and labels. |
| `detail-floating-chat` | minor | desktop | Floating chat or support pill. A fixed bubble in the corner ("Live support", a chat icon) covers content and is a template default. | Put help in the navigation or the footer. If live chat is real, open it from a quiet button the user asks for. |

## imagery

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image-blur-blob` | major | desktop | Blurred colour blob behind the content. Soft coloured orbs in the hero background are decoration without subject. | Remove the blob. If the hero needs an image, use a real photo, product screen or diagram. |
| `image-placeholder-src` | critical | desktop | Stand-in image service. Placeholder or random-photo URLs (placehold, picsum, pravatar ...) show an unfinished page and may disappear. | Replace with the real asset hosted with the site, or remove the slot. |
| `image-avatar-stack` | major | desktop | Overlapping avatar row. A stack of round faces beside "trusted by" is the stock proof device, and the faces are rarely real. | Replace with a named customer quote that can be checked, or remove. |
| `image-no-alt` | minor | desktop | Image without an alt attribute. Screen readers announce the file name instead of the meaning; alt="" marks decoration explicitly. | Write a short description, or alt="" if the image is purely decorative. |
| `image-broken` | major | desktop | Image fails to load. A broken image icon is an obvious defect. | Fix the path or remove the element. |
| `image-poverty` | minor | desktop | Tall page with no real imagery. A long page made only of text and small vector doodles feels generic; SVG decoration does not count as imagery. | Add real photos, product screenshots or video that show the subject (own assets first, then open-licensed with credit). |
| `image-video-no-poster` | minor | desktop | Video without a poster. Until the video loads, the slot is blank. | Add a poster image (and set width and height to avoid layout shift). |

## motion

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `motion-infinite` | major | desktop | Ornament that animates forever. Endless loops (floating shapes, shimmering text, tickers) compete with content and drain batteries. | Animate in response to an action and then stop. Keep infinite loops for real loading indicators only. |
| `motion-entrance-everywhere` | minor | desktop | Everything fades up on load or scroll. Six or more elements entering with the same fade-and-rise turns motion into wallpaper. | Animate one moment (the hero, or one key reveal). Leave the rest still. |
| `motion-no-reduced` | minor | css | No prefers-reduced-motion handling. People who ask the system for less motion still get all of it. | Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) that removes or shortens animations and transitions. |
| `motion-shadow-animated` | minor | css | Shadow animated frame by frame. Animating box-shadow repaints every frame and smears; on a layer that moves away from its base the shadow also ends up in the wrong place. | Put two pre-blurred shadow shapes behind the element (rest and raised) and crossfade their opacity; animate transform and opacity only. |
| `motion-transition-all` | minor | css | transition: all. Animating every property triggers layout work and surprising effects. | List the properties you mean (opacity, transform, background-color) with a duration and easing. |
| `motion-hidden-reduced` | critical | reduced | Content stays hidden when reduced motion is requested. Reveal animations that start at opacity 0 leave the text invisible for people who disable motion. | Make the visible state the default; inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) show everything immediately. |

# Craft (the other number)

Craft score 0 to 100, higher is better; pass mark 70. A page passes only with a clean slop verdict and craft at or above the mark.

| Component | Points | Measures |
|---|---|---|
| hierarchy | 15 | display size against body size, and the number of distinct type steps |
| focal | 15 | one dominant element on the first screen: display headline and/or a large visual |
| visual | 20 | share of the first screen covered by a real visual (product view, image, canvas, drawing) |
| motion | 15 | something moves, inside the visual (a demo, not wallpaper), with reduced motion handled |
| identity | 20 | chosen web font, display face distinct from text face, one accent combination, depth, texture |
| density | 15 | content on the first screen fits the page type (app screens dense, landings balanced) |

## Bland signals

The opposite failure: a page stripped until nothing is left. These never add to the slop score; they explain a low craft score.

| Rule | Severity | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bland-no-hero-visual` | major | No real visual on the first screen. A first screen of text alone asks the reader to imagine the product. Strong pages show it: a product view, a photo, a drawing. | Put the product itself in the first screen: a built UI view, a real screenshot, a photo or a meaningful drawing, at least 8% of the screen. |
| `bland-document-column` | major | Whole page is one narrow column. On a 1440 px screen a single text column from top to bottom reads as a document, not a designed page. | Use the width: put a visual beside the headline, set one section in two or three columns of different weight, or let a product view run wide. |
| `bland-timid-display` | major | No display-size type. On a landing or content page, a title under 2.5x the body size has no voice. Premium pages commit to one large, confident line. (App screens are exempt.) | Set the h1 (or the one hero line) at 2.5x the body size or more, in the display face, with tight tracking. |
| `bland-no-depth` | minor | No depth at all. No shadow, no layered surface, one flat colour everywhere: the page looks like printed paper, not an interface. | Add one layer system: a raised surface for the product view (soft layered shadow), a second surface tone, or one overlapping element. |
| `bland-no-texture` | minor | No texture, pattern or tonal light anywhere. Every surface is one flat fill. Good pages carry a material: grain, a faint pattern or watermark, a tonal light behind the product. | Add one material that suits the project: fine grain, a subtle pattern in one zone, a watermark, or a soft light behind the main visual. Keep it quiet (under 10% opacity). |
| `bland-monochrome` | major | No colour anywhere. Ink on paper with no accent gives the eye no signal for what to press or where the brand is. | Pick one accent with a job (primary action, selection, the key data series) and use it there, consistently. |
| `bland-static` | minor | Nothing moves, even where a demo would explain the product. A product page with a call to action but no motion leaves the reader to guess how the product behaves over time. | Animate the product view once: one short sequence (render(t) or a few keyframes) that shows what happens, then stops. Respect reduced motion. |
| `bland-empty-first-screen` | minor | First screen is mostly empty. Large empty areas with nothing to look at read as unfinished rather than calm. | Fill the first screen with intent: the headline at display size and the product view; keep space around them, not instead of them. |
| `bland-default-serif` | major | Default system serif. Georgia, Times and other built-in serifs are what a browser shows when nobody chose a type face. | Choose a face on purpose (a real web font with a licence that allows self-hosting) and pair it with one text face. |
